dialogues.speaker: Pecherskaya
dialogues.text: You know, I'm actually a pretty generous and open-minded person. I'm not someone who takes offense at every little thing.

dialogues.speaker: Pecherskaya
dialogues.text: As for what happened last time, it certainly wasn't because I had any personal grudge against her. The Golitsyns are hardly the sort of family to fall out with people over trifling matters, are we?

dialogues.speaker: Pecherskaya
dialogues.text: My only concern is that if an employee like her is allowed to speak to passengers that way, especially passengers of our standing, it will reflect badly on the entire Transport Bureau.

dialogues.speaker: Rudov
dialogues.text: After your last complaint about Kholodnaya's conduct, we have reprimanded her and reassigned her to... a position better suited to her.

dialogues.speaker: Rudov
dialogues.text: Of course, if she still can't manage even after that, I'm afraid we'll just have to swallow the bitter pill and let her go.

dialogues.speaker: Pecherskaya
dialogues.text: Very well. She may find such a measure harsh, but I would call it only proper.
